newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Banco Ganadero sees strong first half.
newsitem.headline: Banco Ganadero sees strong first half.

text.p: The head of Banco Ganadero, Colombia's leading commercial bank in terms of assets, said he sees it posting a solid net profit in the first half of 1997 despite the country's steep economic slowdown.
"We're satisfied because no one thought 1997 would get off to such a hard start in terms of the economy," Ganadero's executive president Jose Ayala told a news conference.
He was referring to the fact that Colombia's recession-bound economy posted a second consecutive quarter of negative growth in January-March.

According to Ayala, Ganadero's first-half net profit could total anywhere between 30 billion and 40 billion pesos. If it comes in near the higher end of expectations it would be well above the 31.9 billion pesos reported in the first half of 1996.

For the entire year, Ayala forecast that Ganadero's net would be similar to last year's 56.5 billion pesos, however, largely due to costs associated with increases in its past-due loan provisions. The bank currently has 70 percent of its past-due loans backed by reserves, but Ayala said that would increase to 80 percent by year-end.
